qualification: local A05.3 reliability investigation; not A05.3 closure, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

candidate.scope: Capture the incoming tier-one frame pointer and link register in two existing context words and restore them from that context instead of trusting their generated stack-frame pair. Direct mixed-compiler chaining remained disabled.
candidate.behavioralIntent: Test whether the low-PC production failures were confined to corruption of the tier-one frame-pointer/link-register save pair.
candidate.regressionCoverage: A new encoding test required context-backed tier-one FP/LR capture and restore; the existing tier-one helper-clobber and baseline memory host-control regressions also passed.
candidate.productionFinding: The exact release binary crashed before it could serialize a diagnostic receipt. Control returned from generated code to the correct C caller, but generated execution had violated the Darwin callee-saved contract by returning with x20 changed from the caller's exit-code output pointer to the Swift memory-write callback thunk. The caller's exit-code store therefore attempted a byte write into its read-only executable text segment. Protecting only FP/LR does not contain the production corruption.

verification.deterministicAggregate: 1,556 tests in 179 suites passed with test parallelism disabled.
verification.secondAttemptSkipped: A single host correctness failure rejects a reliability hardening candidate; another full workload run cannot average it into acceptance.

failedRun.esr: Data Abort: byte write Permission fault

retainedBaseline.reason: The behavior-neutral coarse instrumentation remains the last production-safe measurement.

disposition.reason: The candidate is fully reverted. The crash disproves the FP/LR-only corruption hypothesis and positively identifies a separate corrupted callee-saved register. Any future containment must preserve and verify the complete generated-code callee-saved bank before mixed-compiler edge admission resumes.

limitations: The run produced no diagnostic receipt, so guest progress, retired instructions, dispatcher counters, elapsed execution, and workload status are unavailable and are not inferred.
The crash proves x20 was corrupted across generated execution but does not identify the generated instruction, callback, or stack write that first changed its saved value.
Passing directed MAP_JIT tests do not reproduce production cache rotation, predictor history, interrupts, or long native chains.
